app_documentation:
Simple Task Manager is a web-based productivity application designed to help users efficiently track and manage their daily tasks. Built with a modern technology stack including React for the frontend, Node.js/Express for the backend, and PostgreSQL for data persistence, the application provides a clean and intuitive interface for task management. The primary purpose is to enable users to create, organize, complete, and delete tasks while maintaining a clear overview of their work progress through dedicated active and completed task views.

The application features four core capabilities: Task Creation allows users to add new tasks with titles and optional descriptions, with built-in validation to ensure data quality; Task Completion enables users to mark tasks as done and track their accomplishments in a separate completed tasks screen; Task Deletion provides the ability to permanently remove unwanted tasks with safety confirmation dialogs; and Task Listing offers organized views of all tasks with filtering options to focus on active or completed items. Additional features include user profile management, task statistics, and a responsive mobile-first design optimized for touch interactions.

The intended users are individuals seeking a straightforward, no-frills task management solution for personal productivity. The application is designed with accessibility in mind, following WCAG 2.1 AA standards, and features a clean visual design with a primary color scheme of indigo and purple accents. The bottom navigation pattern provides easy access to the main sections: active tasks, completed tasks, and user profile. With its focus on simplicity and core functionality, Simple Task Manager serves users who need an efficient way to track their work without the complexity of advanced project management tools.

The technical architecture follows modern web development best practices with a clear separation between frontend and backend layers. User authentication ensures that tasks are private and associated with individual accounts, while the database schema supports efficient querying through strategic indexing on frequently accessed fields. The application is delivered as a single-page application (SPA) with smooth transitions and micro-interactions that enhance the user experience without sacrificing performance.

glossary.Task: A discrete work item created by a user with a title and optional description that can be marked as complete or deleted. Tasks are the primary data entity in the application and are stored in the tasks table with associated metadata including creation and completion timestamps.
glossary.FAB (Floating Action Button): A circular button positioned in the bottom-right corner of the Task List Home screen that provides quick access to create a new task. The FAB follows Material Design principles and is styled with the primary color and a plus icon.
glossary.Baseline Artifact: A versioned snapshot of project documentation or specifications that serves as a reference point for tracking changes and maintaining governance. Baseline artifacts include requirements, design specifications, database schemas, and development plans.
glossary.Bottom Navigation: A navigation pattern positioned at the bottom of the screen with three tabs (Tasks, Completed, Profile) that allows users to switch between main application sections. This pattern is optimized for mobile devices and thumb-friendly interactions.
glossary.Toast Notification: A temporary, non-intrusive feedback message that appears at the bottom of the screen to confirm user actions such as task creation, completion, or deletion. Toast notifications auto-dismiss after 3 seconds and provide immediate visual feedback.
glossary.Acceptance Criteria: Specific, testable conditions written in Given-When-Then format that define when a feature is considered complete and functioning correctly. Each feature in the application has multiple acceptance criteria that guide development and testing.
